### Issue 1
Title: `[P1] HNSW index permanently invalidated after upsert — O(n) regression`
Body:
```markdown
**Focus area**: RAG & Vector Store
**PRD phase**: Phase 5 — Intelligence/DX/Production (RAG hardening)
**Estimated effort**: S (1 day)
**Labels**: `bug`, `hardening`, `area:rag`, `phase:5-production`

### Problem
After any `Upsert` or `Remove` call, `upsertExample` (`rag.go:1108-1113`) and `removeExample` (`rag.go:1131-1141`) set `s.index = nil` but the lazy-rebuild promise in the comment is **never fulfilled**. `Retrieve` (`rag.go:959`) checks `s.index != nil` to decide HNSW vs brute-force — since the index stays `nil`, every subsequent retrieval falls back to O(n) brute-force for the entire process lifetime.

The comment at `rag.go:1105` says "we rebuild lazily on next Retrieve if needed" but `Retrieve` (`rag.go:928`) has **no rebuild path**: it only reads `s.index` and never calls `rebuildIndex`. The `IndexModeBruteForce` returned by `IndexMode()` after an upsert (`rag_test.go:841`) is therefore **permanent**, not transitional.

### Proposed solution
1. Add a `generation` int64 field to `Store` incremented atomically on every upsert/delete.
2. In `Retrieve`, detect a stale index (`s.index == nil && len(s.examples) >= indexThreshold`) and trigger a synchronous `rebuildIndex()` before the search — or spawn a background goroutine that rebuilds and swaps atomically.
3. Add a `nexus_rag_index_generation` gauge to `/status` so operators can observe when the index was last rebuilt.

A concrete new function: `store.maybeRebuildIndex()` called at the top of `Retrieve` before the `useIndex` decision.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `TestHNSWIndexUpsertThenRetrieve_HNSWPathActive` — after `Upsert`, `IndexMode()` returns `IndexModeHNSW` (not `IndexModeBruteForce`) for stores above `indexThreshold`
- [ ] `BenchmarkRetrieve_AfterUpsert` — p99 latency with 1000 examples after 10 upserts is within 2× of cold-start HNSW Retrieve (not O(n) brute-force)
- [ ] `nexus_rag_index_generation` gauge increments on each upsert/delete
- [ ] `make ci` passes with coverage ≥ 70%

### References
- `internal/rag/rag.go:1105-1113` — upsertExample nil-out + misleading comment
- `internal/rag/rag.go:928-958` — Retrieve, no rebuild path
- `internal/rag/rag_test.go:829-844` — `upsertInvalidatesIndexReportsBruteForce` test documents the broken behavior
- `#420` — HNSW index original implementation
- PRD Phase 5 — RAG hardening
```
Labels: bug,area:rag,phase:5-production

### Issue 2
Title: `[P1] containsWord silently matches all prompts when keyword is empty — routing corruption`
Body:
```markdown
**Focus area**: Routing Intelligence
**PRD phase**: Phase 5 — Intelligence/DX
**Estimated effort**: S (1 day)
**Labels**: `bug`, `area:router`, `phase:5-intelligence`

### Problem
`containsWord` at `dsl.go:171-178` returns `true` for any string when `kw == ""`:

```go
func containsWord(s, kw string) bool {
    if kw == "" {
        return true  // ← matches everything
    }
    pattern := `(?i)\b` + regexp.QuoteMeta(kw) + `\b`
    matched, _ := regexp.MatchString(pattern, s)
    return matched
}
```

`regexp.MatchString("(?i)\\b\\b", "hello")` returns `true` (double word boundary matches at string start/end), so an empty keyword matches every prompt. If any `categoryKeywords` entry ever acquires an empty string, `Categorize` would return the first matching category for **all** prompts — silently corrupting routing for the entire judge-guided adaptive system. No test in `dsl_test.go` or `confidence_test.go` guards against this.

### Proposed solution
Return `false` when `kw == ""` instead of `true`:

```go
func containsWord(s, kw string) bool {
    if kw == "" {
        return false  // empty keyword matches nothing
    }
    // ...
}
```

Add a test case in `dsl_test.go` asserting `containsWord("anything", "") == false` and `Categorize("") != ""`.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `containsWord("anything", "")` returns `false` (not `true`)
- [ ] `Categorize("")` returns `CategoryOther` (not first matching category)
- [ ] Existing `dsl_test.go` and `confidence_test.go` tests pass unchanged
- [ ] `make test-race` passes with coverage ≥ 70%

### References
- `internal/router/dsl.go:171-173` — the buggy guard
- `internal/router/confidence.go:148-157` — `Categorize` calls `containsWord`
```
Labels: bug,area:router,phase:5-intelligence

### Issue 3

- [ ] Counter is observable via `GET /metrics` with no auth required
- [ ] Unit test covers the path: blocked IP → `authBlockedTotal.Inc()` called

### Issue 4
Title: `[P2] PersistentStore.IndexDir bypasses NEXUS_RAG_BATCH_SIZE — silent 31× perf regression`
Body:
```markdown
**Focus area**: RAG & Vector Store
**PRD phase**: Phase 5 — Intelligence/DX/Production
**Estimated effort**: S (1 day)
**Labels**: `bug`, `enhancement`, `area:rag`, `phase:5-production`

### Problem
`NEXUS_RAG_BATCH_SIZE` is wired to `Store` via `WithBatchSize` (`cmd/nexus/main.go:1573,1590`), and `Store.IndexDir` (`rag.go:862-890`) correctly partitions files into batches and calls `EmbedBatch` per batch. However, `PersistentStore.IndexDir` (`sqlite.go:426-506`) **completely overrides** the embedded `Store.IndexDir` and indexes every file individually via a single `Embed` call per file, ignoring `batchSize` entirely.

Result: on a cold boot with 1000 files and `NEXUS_RAG_BATCH_SIZE=32`, the persistent path makes **1000 HTTP round-trips** instead of **32** (a 31× degradation in indexing latency and Ollama load).

### Proposed solution
1. Refactor `PersistentStore.IndexDir` to:
   - Collect all valid files first
   - Partition into batches of `s.Store.batchSize`
   - Call `EmbedBatch` per batch (matching `Store.IndexDir`'s logic)
   - Call `Upsert` per batch within a single SQLite transaction
2. Add `TestPersistentStoreIndexDir_UsesBatchEmbedding` verifying `EmbedBatch` is called (not `Embed`) when `batchSize > 0`.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] With `NEXUS_RAG_BATCH_SIZE=32` and 64 files, `EmbedBatch` is called exactly 2 times (not 64 times)
- [ ] `PersistentStore.IndexDir` with `batchSize=0` continues to call `Embed` once per file (regression test)
- [ ] `nexus_rag_retrieval_total` label `{path="brute_force"}` does not increase after cold-boot indexing completes
- [ ] `make ci` passes with coverage ≥ 70%

### References
- `internal/rag/sqlite.go:426-506` — `PersistentStore.IndexDir` (overrides embedded method)
- `internal/rag/rag.go:862-890` — `Store.IndexDir` (correct batch usage)
- `cmd/nexus/main.go:1573` — `WithBatchSize` wired for persistent store
- `#771` — batch embedding support (PR #781 merged)
```

### Issue 6
Title: `[P2] Confidence routing_outcomes table grows unbounded with no vacuum/cleanup`
Body:
```markdown
**Focus area**: Routing Intelligence
**PRD phase**: Phase 5 — Intelligence/DX
**Estimated effort**: S (1 day)
**Labels**: `hardening`, `area:router`, `phase:5-intelligence`

### Problem
`SQLiteConfidenceStore.RecordOutcome` (`confidence_sqlite.go:170`) inserts into `routing_outcomes` forever. `LocalConfidence` filters by a sliding window (`WHERE timestamp > ?`) but never deletes old rows. With high request volume and a 7-day window, the table accumulates thousands of rows per category. Over months of operation the `.db` file grows with no upper bound and SQLite's query planner may degrade on large tables despite the index on `(category, timestamp)`. The store has no `Close()` path that runs `PRAGMA vacuum`.

### Proposed solution
Add a row-count ceiling with periodic cleanup:
1. A `PRAGMA vacuum` on first open (reclaim space after any prior growth)
2. Every N inserts (e.g., every 1000), delete rows older than `2 * window` as a safety margin
3. Expose `nexus_confidence_store_rows_total` gauge in `routemetrics.go`

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] After 30,000 `RecordOutcome` calls, `routing_outcomes` rows older than `2*window` are deleted
- [ ] `nexus_confidence_store_rows_total` gauge present in `/metrics`
- [ ] `SQLiteConfidenceStore` survives `make test-race` with 10,000-record soak
- [ ] `make ci` passes with coverage ≥ 70%

### References
- `internal/router/confidence_sqlite.go:170-197` — `RecordOutcome` insert path
- `internal/router/confidence_sqlite.go:41-46` — `confidenceQuerySQL` sliding window filter
- `internal/observability/routemetrics.go` — existing SLM cache metrics as a template
```

### Issue 7
Title: `[P2] getSemantic RLock without proactive eviction — stale entries accumulate silently`
Body:
```markdown
**Focus area**: Routing Intelligence
**PRD phase**: Phase 5 — Intelligence/DX
**Estimated effort**: S (1 day)
**Labels**: `enhancement`, `area:router`, `phase:5-intelligence`

### Problem
`getSemantic` at `slm_cache.go:274` acquires `c.mu.RLock()` and scans all live `c.entries` for cosine similarity. Expired entries are skipped for similarity scoring (`now.Sub(entry.stamp) > c.ttl → continue`) but are **never removed** from `c.entries` or `c.expiry`. Since `getSemantic` holds an RLock (readers don't block readers), it cannot call `evictExpired` (which needs a write lock). With low request volume and long TTL, expired entries accumulate indefinitely between `Set` calls. `Stats().Expired` reports them but no metric surfaces this as a Prometheus gauge.

### Proposed solution
Add `Stale()` method to `SLMCache` returning count of expired-but-live entries. In `getSemantic`, if `Stale() > 0` after the scan, dispatch a background eviction signal. Also expose `nexus_slm_cache_stale_entries` gauge in `routemetrics.go`.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `SLMCache.Stale()` returns count of expired-but-not-yet-evicted entries
- [ ] After TTL expiry on a semantic-cache entry, `Stale()` increases by 1 and `/metrics` reflects it
- [ ] `getSemantic` with `NEXUS_SLMCACHE_MAX_STALE=1` triggers proactive eviction on next `Get`/`getSemantic` call
- [ ] Unit test: insert 3 entries, wait past TTL, verify `Stale() == 3` and no eviction yet
- [ ] `make test-race` passes

### References
- `internal/router/slm_cache.go:274-313` — `getSemantic`
- `internal/router/slm_cache.go:184-206` — `evictExpired` (write-lock only)
- `internal/router/slm_cache.go:458-476` — `Stats()` which already computes `Expired`
```
Labels: enhancement,area:router,phase:5-intelligence

### Issue 8
Title: `[P2] Non-progressive fusion Panel does not record FusionOutcomeEvent — observability gap`
Body:
```markdown
**Focus area**: Upstream & Cascade
**PRD phase**: Phase 2 — Observability & Metrics
**Estimated effort**: S (1 day)
**Labels**: `bug`, `area:upstream`, `phase:2-observability`

### Problem
The non-streaming/non-progressive fusion path (`upstream.Panel`) returns only `(cacheHit bool, error)` (line 528 in `upstream.go`). The chat handler (line 1469) only calls `d.ArbiterCacheObserver(cacheHit)` for this path — it never calls `d.FusionOutcomeObserver`, so `FusionOutcomeEvent` (containing `RequestID` and `ArbiterSkipped`) is never recorded for non-progressive fusion. The progressive path (`PanelStreaming`) correctly calls both observers (lines 1451–1463).

This means `fusion_arbiter_skipped` and `fusion_jaccard_similarity` SQLite columns are always zero for requests in the non-progressive fusion path, making the fusion agreement rate dashboard inaccurate.

### Proposed solution
Change `Panel` signature from `(cacheHit bool, _ error)` to `(outcome PanelOutcome, cacheHit bool, _ error)`. Populate `outcome.Similarity` (always 0 for non-progressive since no similarity comparison is done), `outcome.ArbiterCacheHit`, and `outcome.ArbiterSkipped` (always `true` when cacheHit, `false` when arbiter was invoked). Update `chat.go:1478` to call `FusionOutcomeObserver.ObserveFusionOutcome` after the `Panel` call, mirroring the `PanelStreaming` path.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `FusionOutcomeObserver` is called for every non-progressive fusion request with correct `ArbiterSkipped` value (true when cache hit, false when arbiter was invoked)
- [ ] `make test-race` passes
- [ ] `make ci` passes with coverage ≥ 70%

- `internal/upstream/upstream.go:514` — Panel function body (needs outcome tracking)
- `internal/handlers/chat.go:1469` — caller of Panel (needs FusionOutcomeObserver call)

### Issue 9
Title: `[P2] Panel non-streaming function has zero slog visibility for non-cache-hit paths`

```markdown
**Focus area**: Upstream & Cascade
**PRD phase**: Phase 2 — Observability & Metrics
**Estimated effort**: S (1 day)
**Labels**: `enhancement`, `area:upstream`, `phase:2-observability`

### Problem
The `Panel` function (`upstream.go:514`) is the non-streaming/non-progressive fusion path. It has exactly **one** `slog.Info` call — the arbiter cache hit at line 599. There is zero logging for: which panel member succeeded/failed, when the arbiter was invoked (non-cache-hit path), when the arbiter returned empty synthesis, when a panel goroutine panicked (IncPanelPanics is called but not slogged). 1. Panel members completed — `slog.Info("fusion panel: members ready", ...)`
2. Arbiter invoked (cache miss) — `slog.Info("fusion arbiter invoked", ...)`
3. Arbiter returned empty synthesis — `slog.Warn("fusion arbiter returned empty synthesis", ...)`
4. Panel goroutine panic (already calls `IncPanelPanics()`, add slog before it)

Include `requestID string` parameter on `Panel` to enable log correlation (matching `PanelStreaming`'s pattern at `upstream.go:769`).

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `Panel` function has slog.Info/Warn calls for: panel members ready, arbiter invoked, empty synthesis, and panic recovery
- [ ] `requestID string` parameter added to `Panel` signature (matching `PanelStreaming`)
- [ ] All slog calls include `request_id` field for log correlation

### Issue 10
Title: `[P2] APIKeyAwareKeyFunc Bearer-prefix stripping is case-sensitive — fragmented rate limits`
Body:
```markdown
**Focus area**: Security & Auth
**PRD phase**: Phase 5 — Production hardening
**Estimated effort**: S (1 day)
**Labels**: `bug`, `hardening`, `area:ratelimit`, `phase:5-production`

### Problem
At `internal/ratelimit/middleware.go:162`, `APIKeyAwareKeyFunc` uses `strings.TrimPrefix(auth, "Bearer ")`. This only strips the prefix when the Authorization header value begins with exactly `"Bearer "` (capital B, single space). If a client sends `"bearer mykey"` or `"BEARER MYKEY"`, `TrimPrefix` finds no match and the full string — including the scheme — is hashed as the bucket key.

The result: the **same API key** behind the **same IP** occupies **different rate-limit buckets** depending on header casing, fragmenting per-client rate limits unpredictably.

The auth middleware itself is case-insensitive on the scheme (`strings.EqualFold` at `internal/auth/auth.go:142`), so this inconsistency is not caught by auth tests.

### Proposed solution
Replace the case-sensitive `TrimPrefix` check at `middleware.go:162` with a case-insensitive `HasPrefix` + substring extraction:

```go
// Normalise: strip "Bearer " (case-insensitive) so "bearer mykey"
// and "Bearer mykey" produce the same bucket key.
if strings.HasPrefix(strings.ToLower(auth), "bearer ") {
    key = strings.TrimSpace(auth[7:])
}
```

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `APIKeyAwareKeyFunc("10.0.0.1", reqWithHeader("bearer mykey"))` returns the same bucket key as `APIKeyAwareKeyFunc("10.0.0.1", reqWithHeader("Bearer mykey"))`
- [ ] `APIKeyAwareKeyFunc("10.0.0.1", reqWithHeader("Bearer  mykey"))` (double space) also produces the same key
- [ ] `TestMiddleware_APIKeyAwareKeyFunc_CaseInsensitiveBearer` added with all three cases above
- [ ] `make ci` passes with coverage ≥ 70%

### References
- `internal/ratelimit/middleware.go:162` — `strings.TrimPrefix` is case-sensitive
- `internal/auth/auth.go:142` — auth middleware correctly uses `EqualFold` for scheme comparison
- `internal/ratelimit/middleware_test.go:675` — `TestMiddleware_APIKeyAwareKeyFunc_NoAuth` covers missing header, not casing
```
Labels: bug,area:ratelimit,phase:5-production

### Issue 13
Title: `[P2] AuthRateLimit fields missing from YAMLConfig — YAML operators cannot tune brute-force protection`
Body:
```markdown
**Focus area**: Config & Developer Experience
**PRD phase**: Phase 5 — DX/Production
**Estimated effort**: S (1 day)
**Labels**: `enhancement`, `area:config`, `phase:5-dx`

### Problem
`AuthRateLimitRPM`, `AuthRateLimitBurst`, and `AuthRateLimitWindow` (issue #296) are fully implemented in `config.go` (lines 503–505, parsed at lines 1547–1572) and documented in `.env.example` (lines 226–229), but are **absent from `YAMLConfig`** in `yaml.go`. Operators who run with `NEXUS_CONFIG_FILE=config.yaml` cannot set the auth brute-force protection parameters via YAML — the values silently fall through to hardcoded defaults (RPM=5, Burst=3, Window=5m) regardless of what is written in the YAML file.

### Proposed solution
1. Add three fields to `YAMLConfig` in `yaml.go`:
   - `AuthRateLimitRPM int yaml:"auth_rate_limit_rpm"`
   - `AuthRateLimitBurst int yaml:"auth_rate_limit_burst"`
   - `AuthRateLimitWindow string yaml:"auth_rate_limit_window"`
2. Add `env override` blocks in `LoadYAML` mirroring the pattern used for `RateLimitRPM`/`RateLimitBurst`, parsing `NEXUS_AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_RPM`, `NEXUS_AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_BURST`, and `NEXUS_AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW`.
3. Populate defaults in `toConfig()` using the same values as `config.go` defaults (5, 3, 5*time.Minute).
4. Add `env_example_audit_test.go` coverage to ensure the three new `.env.example` entries are tracked bidirectionally.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A YAML file containing `auth_rate_limit_rpm: 10` produces `cfg.AuthRateLimitRPM == 10` when loaded via `LoadYAML`
